proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the defining property of the floor function, \(\lfloor x\rfloor\le x\). Subtracting \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) from both sides gives \(0\le x-\lfloor x\rfloor\). Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x. This directly proves the lemma. The previous feedback is addressed by keeping the proof exactly at the floor-function inequality and not introducing any unrelated fractional-part identity.
solver_summary: For any real x, the floor definition gives \(\lfloor x\rfloor\le x\), hence \(x-\lfloor x\rfloor\ge 0\).
vetter_reason: The proof directly establishes the lemma from the defining property of floor: floor(x) <= x, hence 0 <= x - floor(x). It matches the stated lemma exactly and introduces no unsupported claims or dependency issues.
